title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Consistency in Interactive Narratives
hook: Fluent writing is not the same as staying consistent: the best model keeps its story straight for only 42% of runs past 20 turns of adversarial play.
key_points: Frames the problem as Narrative Commitment Preservation: can an agent honor earlier facts and promises under unconstrained user moves?
NCP-Bench: 100 narrative environments built from movie synopses, each with a checkable spec of trajectory, commitments, and initial facts.
Automatic checking throughout the player-agent vs. narrator-agent interaction, so consistency is graded turn by turn, not just at the end.
Best model (GPT-5.2) survives only 42% of runs past 20 turns; fact-conflict rates run 40-68% across tested models.
Within a 100-turn limit, only isolated runs satisfied every achievement commitment — long-horizon consistency is largely unsolved.
High linguistic quality does not predict commitment preservation: the two are measured separately and come apart.
content_html: Interactive storytelling is a natural fit for LLMs — but a narrator that writes beautifully and then contradicts its own plot is useless. This benchmark separates the two skills and finds that even frontier models lose the thread fast.
extra_html: Yingpeng Ma and colleagues formalize the challenge as Narrative Commitment Preservation: holding logical consistency and narrative integrity together while a user pushes in unconstrained directions. Their testbed, NCP-Bench, is 100 narrative environments derived from movie synopses; each carries a structured specification — the intended trajectory, the commitments the story has made, and its initial facts — that can be checked automatically as a player agent and a narrator agent interact. Across state-of-the-art models the authors report a substantial long-horizon consistency gap: linguistic quality does not guarantee commitment preservation, the best-performing model (GPT-5.2) survives only 42% of runs after 20 turns, fact-conflict rates span 40-68% across models, and within the 100-turn limit only isolated runs satisfied every achievement commitment. Yingpeng Ma and colleagues, arXiv, August 2026.

related.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks
related.hook: 46 terminal tasks that take hours, not minutes — and today's best agent still only nails 15% of them, with the average model managing barely 4%.

related.title: Attractor States Emerge in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations
related.hook: Let two LLMs debate long enough and one model's style pulls the other toward it — Claude Haiku drags partners into its own habits, while GPT-4.1 nano is easily swayed.

related.title: LLMs Get Lost When Intent Keeps Moving
related.hook: Real users don't state what they want up front — they reveal, revise, and redirect it mid-conversation. Rewrite existing benchmarks that way and scores drop across every model family.

flashcards.prompt: What does Narrative Commitment Preservation (NCP) measure?
flashcards.back_html: Whether an agent keeps honoring the facts and commitments it established earlier, even when a user intervenes in unconstrained or adversarial ways over a long interaction.

flashcards.prompt: What survival rate does the best-performing model reach after 20 turns on NCP-Bench?
flashcards.explanation_html: GPT-5.2, the strongest model tested, survives only 42% of runs past 20 turns — and fact-conflict rates range from 40% to 68% across models.

flashcards.prompt: How does NCP-Bench make narrative consistency automatically checkable?
flashcards.back_html: Each of its 100 environments, derived from movie synopses, ships a structured spec — trajectory, commitments, initial facts — that a checker verifies throughout the player/narrator interaction.

flashcards.prompt: What does the paper conclude about the link between linguistic quality and consistency?

choices.text: Fluent output does not guarantee commitment preservation
Models that write well always stay consistent
Consistency improves steadily as conversations get longer

flashcards.explanation_html: The authors report that high linguistic quality does not guarantee commitment preservation: strong models still generate logically conflicting content under adversarial interventions.
